text_fidelity_a:
ALEX Toys Artist Studio My Art Spinner This toy is plenty entertaining for a short while. It is great fun to make the art, and the paint colors are bright and contemporary (neon green, yellow, coral, blue, and purple). The spinner is seemingly durable, powered by one C-cell battery (which is not included).

But, consider --

The bottles of ink are teeny-weeny -- .6 fl oz each -- about the size of a small hotel shampoo bottle. The jars of glitter are even tinier. Although the kit contains glitter, there is no glue to apply it. The glitter seems like a bit of an afterthought. And for some reason, even though there are five colors of paint, spinner device contains only three holes to hold the paint.

The cards to paint on are tiny as well -- there are ten cards that are about 4"x 4" each, and another ten cards that are about 3" x 3". Half are black and half are white. You may be able to make "beautiful art" (says so right on the box) but at 3" x 3", it's hard to make much of a statement.

The kit contains a clear plastic "splash guard" That is labeled in tiny font as such, along with a "do not discard" warning. If you happened to overlook the label, you would likely discard the splash guard, as it is indistinguishable from much packaging.

I have a similar spin-art painter from Crayola, the color spinner -- hard to say which one of these two items would be preferable. This Alex spinner is battery-operated, the Crayola one is not. This Alex spinner definitely has cooler paint colors. The Crayola spinner has circular pieces of cardboard to paint on. They are much larger and the shape is more interesting. Either kit would be fun for kids. Once or twice.

This would be a fun toy to play with once or twice, but I wouldn't expect it to be something you will return to again and again. And if you purchase it, don't forget to get a C-cell battery.
text_fidelity_b: ALEX Toys Artist Studio My Art Spinner

text_fidelity_a:
WowWee - MiP the Toy Robot - White This is a four star product in many ways. But I'm giving it three due to the following factors...

Excellent build quality and hardware features. However, without some additional software and accessories this you won't see lasting use.

Hardware: you WILL need a phone or tablet to unlock the limited potential of this toy. The included gesture and sound functionality is too rudimentary (and yet also hard to acess consistently) for lasting interest. If you don't plan to provide access to a tablet or phone, get WowWee's robotic dog product instead. Although it is easy to set up an obstacle course or seesaw on your own, purpose-built accessories would go a long way towards providing a "fiction" for the toy to inhabit, as well as proven fun activities.

Software: the existing apps are very well made and provide a significant boost to the toys functionality. I'd say about 75%. However, most are of limited scope and soon become repetitive. The best feature is the ability to remotely drive the robot and also record its adventures. I'd like to see a feature that allows kids to rudimentarily program the robot (perhaps to interact with purpose built accessories) not just activate sounds and colored lights... I'd also like to see the toolset opened to adults (Lua scripting?) so that they can extend the functionality for Pre-K through K STEM learning.

I understand trying to hit price points is important. But this is either a $75 toy with a few $25 accessory kits, or a $125 toy all in. The existing package (while decent) is limiting the potential of the product.
text_fidelity_b: WowWee - MiP the Toy Robot - White

Spin Flip Puzzle - Hypnotic - Spin it, Flip it, Solve it! for Those who Love Brain teasers! Adult Fidget Toy. Great Gift for Mom, Dad, Teens, Men and Women I could not tell exactly how these “puzzles” work, even after looking at the video. You have to do two different things. First you have to “flip” each of the circles back-and-forth until you get all of them flipped to the correct side. Then you have to “spin” each of the circles to align them correctly. I find that it’s best to start from the outside circle and work your way in. The “puzzles” with most similar colors / designs on each side are the most challenging to work to get the circles on the correct side.

FYI. . . Once you have completed one side, the opposite side will not be complete. So though you will not have to flip the circles. . You’ll have to rotate the circles to complete the puzzle. So you’ll always have one side complete, and one size incomplete.

It should be noted that this “puzzle” is sturdy enough for a puzzle such as this, but it can certainly be pulled apart and broken without too much effort.

I think this “puzzle” to be best for ages tweens and up. It’s not super challenging, but again the ones with the common colors on both sides are the most challenging.

This puzzle is Made in China and being sold by a Canadian company on Amazon.
text_fidelity_b: Spin Flip Puzzle - Hypnotic - Spin it, Flip it, Solve it! for Those who Love Brain teasers! Adult Fidget Toy. Great Gift for Mom, Dad, Teens, Men and Women

Thames & Kosmos 626020 Pepper Mint in The Great Treehouse Engineering Adventure Science Experiment Kit, Blue We enjoyed using this kit. I did it mostly with my 7 and 10 year old children. My 7 year old was the most interested. My 5 year old had interest, but he wasn't as gentle with it as he needed to be.

I especially like that the projects are centered around a story. You read a little, then build, read, build..... It makes the whole thing more fun and puts things into perspective. Everything you need is provided in the box, except for 2 AA batteries(so have those on hand before starting). The projects can get a little complicated, particularly when the gears come into the story, but it's not too bad. Some children might need help(or it can simply be a challenge to see if they can figure it out on their own).

The quality is mostly nice. The treehouse is made out of sheets of wood, and it seems durable to me. It won't last through rough play, but for the project, it holds up well. When building the treehouse, you can glue the pieces into place. We chose to take it apart, so we could do the projects again later with my youngest child. (Untying the knots was a bit of a pain, but otherwise, it's pretty simple to take apart.) There are a few pieces that are paper, though, and these are much less durable.

If you're looking for a fun project for a rainy day of learning, this is a nice kit to try.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos 626020 Pepper Mint in The Great Treehouse Engineering Adventure Science Experiment Kit, Blue

text_fidelity_a:
Hive- A Game Crawling With Possibilities [[VIDEOID:6e39915180719f8cf806a7bff52071ca]] I hate to say it, because it might scare people off, but this is a lot like chess. But it's a ton more fun than chess, and it takes much less time to learn, so I think you'll like it even if you hate chess. And if you love chess, you'll love this game. It's also a pretty deep strategy game, so if you love strategy games, you'll love this.

Instead of playing on a board, you position your hex pieces adjacent to your opponent's pieces, and then move them around "the hive" (the collection of pieces in the middle), until somebody's queen bee is completely surrounded, and that person loses the game.

Here's a list of the pieces, and what they can do:
*Queen bee, similar to the King in chess. Can only move one space
*Beetle, moves only one space, but can move on top of other tiles (a big advantage)
*Spider, moves three spaces in one direction (the worst piece, in my opinion)
*Soldier ant, moves anywhere outside the perimeter of the hive
*Grasshopper, can only move by jumping over pieces

And, if you want to buy expansion packs, you can get
*[[ASIN:B003WZGDEW Mosquito Expansion]], which clones the ability of pieces it touches
*[[ASIN:B00472O260 Ladybug Expansion]], which moves like the knight in chess. Two on top of the hive, and then one down
*Or, [[ASIN:B00472O26K Hive Carbon]], which is black and white, and has the exact same pieces as this game, plus the pieces in the expansion packs

Pros:
+Very sturdy construction
+You can play on any surface
+Very quick to learn, and even quicker to teach. You could be playing this 5 minutes from now
+Extremely fun strategy game. I love it!
+Even if you hate strategy games, you'll like this. Unless you play with someone better than you that keeps beating you, and then you might not like it too much.

Cons:
-Completely different than any strategy game you've played, so it will take a while to build your strategy
text_fidelity_b: Hive- A Game Crawling With Possibilities

The batteries that make Dora talk to the little cook are already included and inserted in the compartment.

This colorful kitchen is very compact and everything gets conveniently stored inside the roomy refrigerator and oven. The sink is over the refrigerator and the burner and grill is over the oven. Above the sink/stove top is a window and a place to slide in the recipe card, and above this at the top is a shelf. Next to the recipe card is a cell phone holder. Dora stands behind the stove cooktop to the other side.

The recipe card is double sided, with 2 recipes on each side for a total of 4 recipes included. When you slide the card in, you can then press one of two flower buttons that speak to you with directions for your recipe. Sometimes the phone will ring as well and speak to you. There are over 60 phrases in English and Spanish. One side of the card has 2 recipes for a Barbecue- hamburgers and ice cream and the other side of the card has 2 recipes for a Spring Picnic- huevos rancheros and tacos. Step by step, Dora tells the little cook exactly what to do.

All the ingredients and cooking utensils your little chef will need to create these 4 recipes are included. There are 20 play accessories, including: plate, spatula, pan, cup, fork, spoon, phone, salad dressing, milk, hash browns, egg, lettuce, hamburger patty, tortilla, chicken breast, buns, banana and ice creams. Some of the food items are hard plastic and some softer, like the real food.

Your kids will have so much fun learning to create scrumptious dishes with Dora in this wonderful talking kitchen. I'm already looking for more recipe cards for this kitchen and I found a great Holiday Cookies one for this Christmas for them. We've had other play kitchens, but this talking one gets all the play time by both the girls and boys.
text_fidelity_b: Fisher-Price Dora Fiesta Favorites Kitchen

Classic Yahtzee, An Exciting Game Of Skill And Chance for age 8 and up In the 50's and 60's Board Games and Cards were very popular. I remember playing Yahtzee in the 60's mainly with older family than with friends. The older people in the 50's and 60's loved cards- my Mother's friends had Bridge Clubs and the men loved their Poker Nights. I always felt Yahtzee was a combination of a board type game using dice combined with the skill of cards.

The object of Yahtzee is to get the most points by figuring out the points the dice will give you with 3 of a kind, large straight, full house, aces and other card type combinations. You get three chances to roll the most points you can figure out. You really had to figure out which dice would get you more points on the upper section or the lower section of your score card to score high. They even included chips in the game, as you could get a chip for every 100 points you score.

When you roll the 5 dice all the same number, that was Yahtzee. It's nice to see Classic games coming around again to enjoy. For anyone who likes the strategy of playing cards, only with rolling 5 dice, Yahtzee brings that and more to this classic 50's game of both skill and chance.
text_fidelity_b: Classic Yahtzee, An Exciting Game Of Skill And Chance for age 8 and up

text_fidelity_a:
Educational Insights Hot Dots Let's Learn Pre-K Reading - Learn to Read Preschool Workbook with Interactive Pen, Kids Travel Activity, Ages 3+ We are really loving these Hot Dots learning activity books. My preschooler loves letters, so this reading book is great for getting some practice in. I love that it covers what you’d expect with matching letters, but also includes other things like rhyming, what happens next themes, letters that start and end in certain sounds, as well as other concepts.

Two areas of improvement: The Pen—My child tends to hold it in the middle or more toward the top, and the sound button always seems to get turned off. I don’t really know of a better placement for this button, but it’s worth mentioning. Maybe one of those slider buttons would be better at preventing the sound being turned off so easily.

The dots themselves don't seem very small, but still seem to cause us some issues when in use. Since the pen is quite large, my kiddo will often choose the right answer, put the pen down on the dot, but miss the dot slightly which then gives us a red light and a “sad” beep. Even though the answer is right, missing the dot makes you think that you’re wrong because you get the red light and sad sound. I then have to say “try that dot again” and reassure that the answer is correct. I do wish the dots were just a little bit larger to give the pen a broader area to make contact with the dot. It's not a major issue, as most of the time we do hit the dot just fine, but it's also something I've noticed that has happened several times.

Otherwise, these books are awesome, very educational and a lot of fun! More of 4.5 Stars for us.
text_fidelity_b: Educational Insights Hot Dots Let's Learn Pre-K Reading - Learn to Read Preschool Workbook with Interactive Pen, Kids Travel Activity, Ages 3+

text_fidelity_a:
Cheerson CX-10 Mini 2.4G 4CH 6 Axis LED RC Quadcopter Toy Drone This is so awesome and it works! I thought that with how affordable it is, that it wouldn't even be able to get off the ground, but it flies great! I have to warn you that it's super hard to fly, though. This will frustrate pretty much everyone except for someone who's already an expert in quad copters. But, it's an awesome first copter to practice on. I felt that I built my skills a lot with this, and now I can fly my bigger copter a lot better than I did before I played around with this.

An awesome thing about this is that you can separately order every part of this copter. And, unlike many electronic devices, the sum of the parts is about the same as getting a new one. So, I guess you could also just get two, and when one breaks, then fix it with the other one. Or wait for them to both break and then Frankenstein a whole one back together. But, because these have such available and interchangeable parts, then I can't give it less than five stars.

The battery lasts for about five minutes of flying. Or, fifteen minutes if you're like me, and get it stuck a lot. And, the blades are all plastic, but they hurt if they run into a person. This is also really easy to get stuck on top of a roof or in a tree, so I recommend flying it in a pretty open field. They do pretty good at crash landings, too, as long as they land on grass, which was most of my landings.

It is packaged with a bunch of replacement blades, too, so you don't have to worry about breaking a few of them. They're easy to replace, too.

This listing has both the CX-10 and CX10A. The only difference is that if you depress the left stick three times on the 10A, then you go into headless mode, which is better for beginners. Anbalulu Magnetic Tiles for Kids, Stacking Blocks, Preschool Stem Construction Building Set 100 Pcs These building elements are a lot of fun! They'll be easy to play with even for the littler kids, and they're colorful, sturdy and simple. Magnets are just perfect - strong enough to hold blocks securely, while not so strong that they'd pinch little fingers, though really small kids might need help with initial separation and pulling of the blocks out of the box. Even a taller construction held up solidly and didn't distort. The set comes with two wheeled bases as well, and as a bonus those can be connected into a train. The wheels move freely, and everything has a quality feel to it.

There's also a little booklet with some basic shapes to build that go gradually from the baby simple to the more complex shapes. A kid could figure them out on their own easily and learn along the way.

The box came chock-full of building elements. I'm not kidding, it's like a puzzle in there - don't expect to be able to figure out how to get it all back in after you take them out. (This is actually kinda nice, because it makes the set very easy to transport without worry of anything shaking up and breaking. Just be aware that it's heavier than expected... I'm taking this to nieces kids by plane, and will have to throw out another thing to stay under the weight limit. That's a lot of magnets.)

The stained glass effect of colors is so pretty, I'm really tempted to get another set for my inner kid, to build a lamp shade with. :-)

UPDATE: The 5 year old I gave this to is still completely in love with it, months later. I had to buy another set for his little cousin who was very upset he didn't get one too.

The bowl itself is smaller than I was expecting, but I actually like that better. It takes up less room. I think it will disappoint some, though. It comes with 10 different colored fish. The bowl is similar to a piggy bank. Your little one puts the fish in through the top, and can only get them out by unplugging the bottom.

The fish will only go in facing forward. This was frustrating to my little ones at first, but they got the hang of it. The hole on the bottom to get the fish out is also a little frustrating to them. It’s on the small side, and they seem to want to get all the fish out at once. This feature teaches them patience and motor skills, I suppose.

Your little one can simply put the fish in the top and have the color told to them by the bowl, or it can be played as a game where the bowl asks for a specific color to be put inside.

Overall, this is a fun and simple learning game.
text_fidelity_b: The Learning Journey: Learn With Me - Color Fun Fish Bowl - Color Teaching Toddler Toys & Gifts for Boys & Girls Ages 2 Years and Up - Preschool Learning Toy, Multicolor

LeapFrog Scout's 3-In-1 Get Up and Go Walker, Green [[VIDEOID:a8db07887b7a7922c5e8d2057fc70226]] This activity panel can be used flat on the floor or attached to wheels. When attached to the wheels, the activity panel can be rotated to either dangle over a baby lying on their back or so a toddler can use it standing or as a walker. You can adjust how freely the wheels move, either slow or fast depending on how competent the child is at walking. The panel has a variety of things: a door to open and close, things to rotate that also rattle, gears, a mirror, a book panel to flip back and forth, and piano keys to touch for sounds or music. You can choose a setting for music, a setting for phrases, or a walking setting. (Requires 2 AA batteries, which were included.) We are using this with a baby lying on their back, and we have removed the phone from reach because it comes (falls) off so easily. The phone is basically a rattle.

The activity panel is 14" wide x 13.5" tall (or 16" if you include the handle). The handle is 9" wide. The wheel assembly measures 20" from front to back (wheel to wheel direction) and 15.5" from the floor to the top (just above the screw). They say to rotate the screws until you hear a click, however I screwed them as tight as I reasonably could and never heard a click. This makes me nervous that they are not on tight enough, and I'll probably ask a man to tighten them when we are using it as a walker. You press a button to release the screw lock so you can unscrew and adjust the angle of the activity panel. Overall, this seems like a nice activity panel. I don't know how effective it is as a walker yet.
text_fidelity_b: LeapFrog Scout's 3-In-1 Get Up and Go Walker, Green

text_fidelity_a:
Chutes and Ladders Board Game Like many of us over 40, we grew up with this game and recognize the graphics of the Classic Chutes and Ladders Board Game. Recently, after my dad passed, we cleared out our old house and found my old game. It followed my brother home to his family, but now I'm curious to compare the two.

Outside of nostalgia, the question is if the game stands on its own in 2015. My four year-old boy thinks so. He doesn't care about 1972 (or even know it existed, as time began with him, as he sees it). He begs to play it, right along with Trouble! and Legos.

Essentially, there's no strategy. The person going version has a small chance of winning, but for all intents and purposes, it is pure chance.

To move forward, the player spins from 1-6. Whatever square he might land on is either neutral, a ladder or a slide. Slides move him back to an earlier square, ladders move him up, and neutral squares allow him to stay put until the next move. There is no decision making.

Is it fun? Very much so, according to my boy. As there are 100 squares, there are plenty of opportunities to climb ladders and slide down. It is a little tricky to follow which direction to go, as the numbers start left-to-right, but zig-zag at each end. A patient older child or adult needs to be on-hand to help with game play.

Anthony Trendl
anthonytrendl.com
text_fidelity_b: Chutes and Ladders Board Game

My Critter Catcher - Spider and Insect Catcher So I know that spiders are generally good, in that they eat other bugs. But they are also terrifying because they are FAST and HIDE BEHIND THINGS, just waiting to attack! Trying to remove them with a cup and piece of paper is perilous at best (what if it GETS OUT and gets on my hand?? I would flail in terror and then who knows where it would land?). So, to defend myself from these miniature terrors, I bought this.

I knew my time had come when my cats were staring at the floor. It was my nemesis, a spider. I tore the catcher out of the packaging and - with only a little shrieking - successfully subdued the spider! It was caught in the bristles, unable to escape! And I was at a safe distance, unlike the cup method where I'd be practically touching the spider. I darted outside and released it. I told the spider he was evicted and to eat bugs outside, never inside. If it ever does venture inside aagin, I know my cat sentries would alert me to its presence and - with minimal shrieking - I could safely evict it again.

My Arcade GameStation Wireless - Plug and Play Game Console - 2 Wireless Controllers - 300 Retro Style Games - Battery or USB Powered - Plugs Into TV I like this game console, but really just think it's something that a few people will enjoy more than most. The design of the console is really good, the look of the main unit is very well done. The wireless controllers are decent enough and feel well made. It's the games though that count. The games are a bit underwhelming. There is a good variety of games, from card games (solitaire, go fish, and a few others of that kind) to puzzle games (sudoku, sliding block puzzle, a pattern block puzzle). There are also many arcade style games. This model of the console does not have any of the old Data East arcade games on it. There is another version that does. The front of the box for that one will have graphics showing the Data East games.

I was sort of expecting the games on this to be the same as what is on most of these sort of consoles (famiclone games), but instead these are a bit more generic than even those. Some of the games are difficult to figure out, it took me about 10-15 minutes or experimenting to figure out how the controllers worked with the sudoku game, and even after I did - the controls were so awkward it made playing the game nearly impossible (and given that this game is timed, I never could achieve a decent time in solving the puzzle). Still, there are many that are worth playing. I think one of the reasons I like game systems like this is the challenge of figuring out what makes the game work.

The main game unit take four double A batteries and the wireless units take triple-A batteries (three each). The console hooks to the TV via a composite video cable (yellow RCA plug) and has one audio input (another RCA plug). I'm using the front inputs on my old VCR which is still connected to my television. I like that the controllers are wireless. You don't really need both, many of the games are for single player. The controllers are marked (P1 & P2), as the P1 controller is the main one and it is used to select the games from the menu.

All-in-all, I am enjoying most of these games, and appreciate the game system for what it is - but I would imagine that many people might not.

This system is made by My Arcade Gaming, and I have one of their handheld Go Gamer Portable games which I purchased last year around Christmas time. I was sort of hoping that this new game console would have the same set of games on it that their handheld model has (which are really good by the way), but that wasn't the case.
text_fidelity_b: My Arcade GameStation Wireless - Plug and Play Game Console - 2 Wireless Controllers - 300 Retro Style Games - Battery or USB Powered - Plugs Into TV

text_fidelity_a:
Tedco 4D Vision Horse Model I bought this model for my 7 year old grandson who recently started riding and currently aspires to be a Vet. The model is small and some of the bits are tiny but manageable if one has reasonable dexterity. It is not for the easily frustrated as it requires patience and a thought to put together. The documentation is marginally helpful, and we used the picture on the cover more that we did the provided sheet for guidance. I also bought "Horse Anatomy (Dover Nature Coloring Book)" which proved a useful addition.
I worked with my grandson to put the model together for the first time. One of the small pieces had molding flash still attached which prevented it from fitting properly until the excess material was removed. The pieces will all fit together properly, but the final assembly is not terribly robust.
To reiterate, it was a bit of a problem solving exercise to fit the pieces into the correct spots, but we found the feeling of accomplishment worth the effort. I do not recommend this as a quick-assembly toy. There are better choices for that purpose. However, I do recommend it as a learning exercise for the curious child. It was fun to see my grandson made associations with his dog and human anatomy during the process. The finished product is suitable for display in a safe spot and can be disassembled and reassembled as long as one keeps track of all the pieces (you wouldn't want to lose his pancreas, would you?). I deducted a star for the less than great documentation.
text_fidelity_b: Tedco 4D Vision Horse Model

Once we got over that hurdle, and a few extra practice rounds, we both just loved it!

There’s enough components to build 2 towers per face-off challenge—each side includes 1 flat thick cardboard tray, 4 plates and 4 cups (all of that x2 for the whole game). The card shows the order in which the tower needs to built for each round, and the first person to build it without it falling over dings the tea pot bell as the winner. The tea pot bell isn’t very pronounced in its sound, which is a good thing that it’s not too loud, but a little underwhelming when you’re excited to ring the bell when you win! It's just a charming design for a stacking and pattern recognition game, and it's definitely fun! Five stars!

text_fidelity_a:
KidKraft Deluxe Let's Cook Kitchen, Gift for Ages 3+ It really is all it's cracked up to be! I have been eyeing it for almost two years and I got lucky and found it in November for $120. I waited to put it together until the night Santa stopped by our house. It did take a few hours to assemble but my husband never left his recliner. I only needed an extra set of hands once or twice and my mom easily did the job.

The top is tricky to attach because the freezer and microwave doors have a tendency to want to leap off the kitchen. I definitely recommend assembling on carpet--the freezer door fell off while I were attaching the top (it's totally stable after the top is attached) and my hardwood floors dinged the corner when the door landed.

If I had to put the kitchen together again, I would definitely get an Allen wrench drill-bit for my drill. The two types of Allen screws in the box have the same head so you can take one of them to the hardware store to ensure the proper drill bit fit. Using a low-power drill makes furniture assembly fast and SO much more pleasant. :)

My son loves it!!! He was only 18 months at Christmas so I was worried he wouldn't know what to do with a kitchen. To my surprise, he ran right to the stove and started turning knobs. He tested the sink handles to make sure they turned and then he started cooking! I totally recommend the utensils and stainless pots & pans from Ikea (they fit the burners perfect). The Melissa & Doug wooden pantry and fridge foods are awesome, as well. Very, very cute.

All-in-all, I am completely delighted with the quality and playtime potential this kitchen offers. My baby might not have any idea what I am talking about when we play "Iron Chef", but he knows how to stir, flip, move things to the sink and move food from the fridge to the microwave to the oven...

Oh, also, my big little guy is 33" already and he has to stand on his tip-toes to see inside his stock pot. He will be cooking for many years to come.
text_fidelity_b: KidKraft Deluxe Let's Cook Kitchen, Gift for Ages 3+

text_fidelity_a:
Melissa & Doug Giant Cheetah - Lifelike Stuffed Animal (Stands Nearly 3 Feet Tall) This unyielding, oversized beast hangs out in my daughter's room and watches her while she sleeps. It has given me pause a couple of times because it has a very serious, fierce Cheetah face. Angry even. This isn't your garden variety Beanie Boo or cute puffy kitty plush. This is a predator and it lets you know it.

Way back when I was a kid, back when we wore newspapers around our feet instead of shoes to trudge to school in 18 feet of snow, I had a panther like this. It was all black and scary enough to send the house cat running full speed out of the room with a puffy tail. I loved my Bagheera so dearly, like my daughter loves this Cheetah. Some sort of magic happens when little girls receive a giant stuffed cat for the Christmas of their 8th year. Alas, my Bagheera crossed the stuffed animal Rainbow Bridge many years ago, but he will always be fondly remembered.

I am very happy that my daughter is also able to shower her love on a giant, regal stuffed animal like I did as a kid, when we lived without electricity or indoor toilets, and my only source of heat was snuggling with my stuffed wild cat. I always took my Bagheera to the outhouse with me in the dead on the night to scare off the wolves, coyotes, and wild boar. That I am here writing this today is evidence that my stuffed cat had a huge impact on my young life. I have no doubt that this Cheetah would also do a great job of deterring bears and badgers on a late night stroll to use the toilet. Thankfully my daughter will never have to deal with such harrowing circumstances, but nevertheless, even if its only job is to sit in a room looking majestic, I highly recommend that you gift this Cheetah to a lucky kid.
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug Giant Cheetah - Lifelike Stuffed Animal (Stands Nearly 3 Feet Tall)

text_fidelity_a:
Disney Hedbanz, 2nd Edition Picture-Guessing Family Board Game, for Adults and Kids Ages 7 and up (Styles May Vary) Got this for adults in family to play. 2 to 6 people play. No one had played before so we were learning strategies as we played. The only time limit is the one minute timer each person has in front of them when it is their turn to ask questions.

To start, a plastic adjustable headband apparatus is given to each player; maximun of six players. Tokens are passed out, 3 per person, one card is dealt to each person that is kept face down and not read; each player takes their one card and place it in the headband on their head so it faces out towards the other players. Do not have mirrors or reflective items nearby so no one can accidentally see their card. If a player leaves the table for a moment, they remove the card and place it face down on the table and return the card to the headband when they return, being careful not to read the card. In addition, a card of helpful questions is passed out to each player to help them ask meaningful questions to get critical answers so they can correctly guess who/what they are on their card.

Rules say the tallest person starts the game, but you have the freedom to start it in any way and play continues to the left. It is also extremely helpful to have a sheet of paper with pen or pencil so you can record answers to the questions you ask. It is hard to remember what questions you previously asked and valuable time is wasted if you are repeating questions that were already answered. We also learned great questions to ask as each player asked their own questions. The players answer with "I don't know", Yes, No, Could be, according to their knowledge of the question. Try to think before you answer and be sure you know the answer because that is critical to the player getting the correct information.

We played this game a lot and got better with each game as we learned how to ask very "to the point" questions. For instance, to start the game, you want to find out if you are a person (George Washington), place (the Great Wall of China) , or thing (jalapeno), (3 separate questions) and each time the other players will answer you with Yes, No, Could Be or Don't know. If you are a person, are you alive or dead? are you fictional (James Bond) or real (John Travolta); am I female or male; am I old or young, etc. The little hint cards do not give you all these options; you have to figure out how to ask your questions in a meaningful way. Each person asks questions until the sand in the timer runs out and play passes to the next person to the left. Keep going around the table until someone guesses their card correctly, and they win and surrender one token. A new round with new cards is started. Rounds are played until someone wins the most rounds and all their tokens surrendered.

You can surrender your card and get a new card and be penalized by receiving an additional token from "the bank" if your questioning is not getting you anywhere, or just start over from the beginning with your questioning because you may have misunderstood an answer that is leading you in the wrong direction. But we usually stuck it out and re-asked questions to find the correct path.

It is a very challenging game; you must be able to think out your progression of questions to reach a conclusion before anyone else. The first player to surrender all their tokens wins the game. The more we played, the better we got at asking questions and the faster we could complete a game, although it could be as long as 45 minutes. A very lively and intriguing game and highly recommended. It could be frustrating but keep a cool head and focus on "how" to ask critical questions. We will play it at all future get togethers and I can't wait until we do.
text_fidelity_b: Disney Hedbanz, 2nd Edition Picture-Guessing Family Board Game, for Adults and Kids Ages 7 and up (Styles May Vary)

Comes with 3 plain dresses, and 3 (pink, yellow, and blue) washable paints, a dress form, and the spinner.
Just place dress on the dress form, place inside spinner, add a drop or two of whatever color you want while pumping the spinner. Out comes a sort of tie-dyed colored dress.
Just wash out the paint, let it dry, and it's all ready to be redesigned once again.
What's really nice is that no batteries are needed. Big plus in my book.

They are using other dresses to paint. It works but, doesn't look as nice as just a plain dress. Anyone who can sew can easily make up a whole wardrobe of clothes that can be spun painted.
Can't complain about the price because this does come with a doll.
Nice toy and would make a great birthday/holiday gift.
I do wish it came with more colors than 3 but, these will do.

HobbyZone Champ RTF, HBZ4900 This is a great little plane, no question. But I ignored Hobbyzone's recommendation for 14 years old and up. I bought two: one for each of my 9-year-old twin sons, who were hot to fly RC model airplanes. One learned to fly quickly, but the other has been seriously disappointed. And I had to learn quickly how to use styrofoam glue to reattach broken wings, tail parts, motor mounts, etc.

It took me a while to understand how critical the trim really is: a beginner really can't fly a plane that isn't trimmed properly. You can get the trim in the ballpark with visual inspection of the control surfaces, but to get it right you have to fly the plane yourself. When I did that, and touched up the trim, flying became a lot of fun - for one boy. The other boy still can't fly more than a few seconds before landing his plane on its nose. He has just about given up in disgust.

I suspect that in a year or two both boys will have good flying skills. But in the meantime one boy is ready to move up while the other is ready to give up. Bummer!
text_fidelity_b: HobbyZone Champ RTF, HBZ4900

Kiddieland Mickey Deluxe Trike, Ride on Building this was a real pain. Let me set this correctly. I review a LOT of toys, many of which need to be assembled. I have the correct tools, I hand tighten the screws, I know what I am doing.
As I built this, getting some of the screws in place was painfully difficult. The parts did not appear to be bent or warped. Putting the 4th screw into the seat (as a random example of this) took some force, then, as I hand tightened the screw, I could feel it thread. I took it out and looked for a spare. There are no spares! So I sourced one from my supply, and with a lot of force got it in place.
If you can fight through all of the battles of assembling this, you end up with a good toy, it works well, easy to control as a parent, easy to move control to junior. But this one is not a fun build!
text_fidelity_b: Kiddieland Mickey Deluxe Trike, Ride on

text_fidelity_a: Alex Art Paintbrush Set 50 Brushes Kids Art Supplies I don't know if each bag contains the same thing, but my bag of "Artist Studio 50 Paint Brushes" had 18 sponge brushes of various sizes, 7 blenders (probably for pastels/chalks), 4 paint brushes (for painting gesso or large areas), 4 bristle brushes (usually for oil paints), 11 nylon brushes (acrylic, oil, watercolor), and 7 animal hair brushes (usually watercolor). The brushes contain a variety of flat and round type brushes of various sizes. Animal hair brushes tend to shed hairs, so don't expect them to last long if kids are using them. However, the rest of the brushes look sturdy enough to withstand some abuse at the hands of kids and will be usable for a while if properly cleaned. They look of equal quality to the brush sets you can buy at a general store (like Walmarts), and the price is good for 50 (or 51) brushes.
text_fidelity_b: Alex Art Paintbrush Set 50 Brushes Kids Art Supplies
